Scientists have said that, so far, earthquakes have been the most devastating of all natural disasters. Earthquakes happen where there are fault lines. A fault line is created by rocks that shift along cracks in the earth's crust. This means that the rocks beside each other are pulled apart. Many people have heard of the San Andreas Fault which is a long and wide fault in the state of California.

In countries such as Iran, Guatemala, Chile, and Japan massive earthquakes have often been recorded. Two of the biggest earthquakes that have ever taken place were in Alaska and China. These earthquakes measured over 8.5 on the Richter scale, which is the instrument used to measure earthquakes. Charles Richter, who was a seismologist, invented the scale in 1935.

On the Richter scale an earthquake that measures 2 or less is considered minor, but earthquakes that measure 7 and above are considered very dangerous and cause heavy damage.
It is important to predict when and where earthquakes will occur. Since the beginning of the twentieth century, Japan, the US and other countries have been actively assessing earthquake activity. In earthquake-prone areas they have established networks that look for warning signs that help predict the time when an earthquake is imminent.

There are other types of instruments that are used to detect activity in the earth's crust. One of these instruments which is called a seismograph, from the Greek word seismos meaning earthquake, can detect movement in the earth thousands of miles away.
Seismologists have already been successful in their prediction of earthquakes in Russia and other parts of the world. However, it has been difficult to predict all earthquakes because new and more up-to-date detecting methods haven't been found yet. Early prediction may help areas prepare for an earthquake and limit its damage.

The Present Perfect and Time Words
You use the Present Perfect tense to talk about past events or actions that began in the past but have a connection to the present.
There are certain “time” words that you usually use in sentences with the Present Perfect tense.
